prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Houston, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1214; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident details, if that's okay.

Q: Understood. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?

A: I was driving on a main road in Houston, Texas, heading toward the freeway entrance. Traffic had slowed down ahead of me.

Q: What happened next?

A: I came to a stop behind a car at a red light. Then I felt a hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and my car got pushed forward into the intersection.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No, I was looking at the light and my mirror was pointed at the car ahead. I didn't see it coming at all.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle afterward?

A: Yes, but my right wrist hurt right away. I was holding the steering wheel with that hand when it happened, and the pain got worse over the next hour.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?

A: Yes. I went to the emergency room that evening. They took X-rays and told me the wrist was fractured. I've been in a splint since then and I have a follow-up appointment with an orthopedic specialist.

Q: Were there any other injuries?

A: My neck was sore for a few days, but it has improved. Mostly it's the wrist that's keeping me from working and doing everyday tasks.

Q: Thank you. Is there anything you'd like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I'm willing to provide my medical records if you need them.

Q: Thank you for your time. This concludes the recorded statement.
